the antihypertension effect of ACE inhibitors is associated with a decrease in cardiac MAO activity and an increase in cardiac noradrenaline content.
the antihypertensives captopril, candesartan, and enalapril increase cardiac catecholamime concentrations and reduce MAO activity via an AT(1)-receptor-mediated mechanism.

the role of AT(1) stimulation on cardiac catecholaminergic function.
the effects of ACE inhibition on cardiac sympathetic function and the role of AT(1) and ANG receptors.

ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor antagonists may increase cardiac sympathetic activity by decreasing MAO activity and increasing cardiac catecholaminergic stores.
